message.content:
Feature build in /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router + Prisma). Add **attention-count badges to the sidebar nav** so operators see at a glance when items need action (unread live chats, open support tickets, open abuse alerts, new feedback). Do NOT touch prisma/schema.prisma. Do NOT run git. Keep the existing visual style.

Context:
- The sidebar is `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (shared by both portals). It takes `nav: NavSection[]`. The admin nav is defined in `app/admin/layout.tsx`; the customer nav in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`. Nav items look like `{ label, href, icon }`.
- Read Shell.tsx, app/admin/layout.tsx, app/dashboard/layout.tsx, and the relevant Prisma models (ChatConversation/ChatMessage, the support ticket model, AbuseAlert, Feedback model, Notification) to learn the exact fields/status enums.

Do this:
1. In Shell.tsx, extend the nav item type with an optional `badge?: number`. When `badge` is a positive number, render a small rounded count pill (e.g. `bg-brand-500 text-white text-[10px] font-semibold rounded-full px-1.5 min-w-[18px] h-[18px]`) right-aligned in the nav row (use `ml-auto`). Don't render anything when badge is 0/undefined. Keep it tasteful and consistent with the existing nav styling; make sure it works for both the active and inactive item states and on mobile.
2. In `app/admin/layout.tsx` (a server component), compute counts and attach them to the matching nav items:
   - Live chat: count of ChatConversation that are OPEN and need a reply / have unread customer messages (match how the admin chat page computes "unread"/"needs a reply" — read `app/admin/chat/page.tsx` and `components/admin/ChatInbox.tsx` / `lib/actions-chat.ts` to use the SAME definition).
   - Support desk: count of open/awaiting-reply support tickets (read the support admin page for the exact status).
   - Abuse queue: count of AbuseAlert with status OPEN.
   - Feedback: count of new/unread feedback (read the admin feedback page for the field).
   Only set `badge` on the items whose count > 0. Use efficient `db.*.count()` queries wrapped in a single `Promise.all`. Gate each count so a missing model/table fails soft (try/catch → 0) — never break the layout.
3. In `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` (customer): add a badge to the **Support** nav item for the count of the customer's own open tickets awaiting a staff reply (their userId only). Keep it minimal; only if the ticket model supports it cleanly.
4. The header already has a notification bell with an unread count — do NOT duplicate that; this is specifically about per-nav-item badges.

Verify: `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` is clean for your files, and `npm run build` exits 0. Report exactly which files you changed and the count logic you used for each badge.

Both checks pass. Verification complete.

## Summary

Added per-nav-item attention badges. Build exits 0 and `tsc --noEmit` (filtered) is clean.

### Files changed

**`/opt/nxeon/components/portal/Shell.tsx`**
- Extended the nav item type: `items: { label; href; icon; badge?: number }[]`.
- In the nav row, render a right-aligned pill when `badge` is a positive number: `ml-auto flex h-[18px] min-w-[18px] items-center justify-center rounded-full px-1.5 text-[10px] font-semibold`. Inactive items use `bg-brand-500 text-white`; active items use `bg-white/25 text-white` so the pill stays legible over the active gradient. Nothing renders when badge is 0/undefined. Counts over 99 show `99+`. Works on mobile since it's inside the same `.nav-item` flex row.

**`/opt/nxeon/app/admin/layout.tsx`**
- Added a single `Promise.all` of four `db.*.count()` queries, each wrapped in a `soft()` helper (`.catch(() => 0)`) so a missing model/table fails soft. Badges are merged into `visibleNav` by matching `href`, only when count > 0.

**`/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/layout.tsx`**
- Added one soft `db.ticket.count()` scoped to the current user, attached to the `/dashboard/support` nav item only when > 0.

### Count logic used

- **Live chat** (`/admin/chat`): `chatConversation.count({ where: { unreadForAgent: true } })` — the same "needs a reply / unread" signal `app/admin/chat/page.tsx` sorts and counts by (`unreadCount = rows.filter(c => c.unreadForAgent)`).
- **Support desk** (`/admin/support`): `ticket.count({ where: { status: { in: ["OPEN", "CUSTOMER_REPLY"] } } })` — matches the page's "Awaiting staff" stat (`open + CUSTOMER_REPLY`). `TicketStatus` enum: OPEN / ANSWERED / CUSTOMER_REPLY / CLOSED.
- **Abuse queue** (`/admin/abuse`): `abuseAlert.count({ where: { status: "OPEN" } })` — matches the page's `open` filter.
- **Feedback** (`/admin/feedback`): `feedback.count({ where: { status: "NEW" } })` — untriaged reports needing action. (The page's own header "open" stat is broader — NEW/PLANNED/IN_PROGRESS — but PLANNED/IN_PROGRESS are already being worked, so NEW is the correct "needs attention / new" signal for a badge. `status` is a String field: NEW | PLANNED | IN_PROGRESS | DONE | DECLINED.)
- **Customer Support** (`/dashboard/support`): `ticket.count({ where: { userId: user.id, status: { in: ["OPEN", "CUSTOMER_REPLY"] } } })` — the customer's own tickets awaiting a staff reply.
